name: Casa de Estudillo

dates.altered: Abandoned in 1887 and 'reduced to a ruin in the course of twenty three years'; restored in 1910 for John D. Spreckels to designs by Hazel W. Waterman, who, the survey says, 'endeavored to rebuild the house to as near the designs of the original as photographs showed' but changed roof ridge lines and window locations (survey).
dates.note: The Wikipedia infobox prints 'Built 1827'; the 1930s survey prints 'Date of erection: 1825'. Both recorded; neither changed. What stands is substantially a 1910 reconstruction on the survey's own account.

quotes.text: Materials of construction: foundation probably of stone laid in adobe mortar, as was the custom of that period. Walls of sun-dried adobe brick, laid in adobe mortar and plastered both sides.
quotes.page: First sheet; no page number printed.

quotes.text: Roof framing of undressed eucalyptus logs connections fastened with raw- hide thongs. Over the roofs of corridors are laid mats of caresa, a material much like bamboo, obtained from the Cuyamaoa lake region, several miles north of Oldtown. Over this is laid the roof tile. New posts and lintel framing of porfches is of milled and dressed lumber. Solid one-inch rough boarding cover the rafters of the house proper. Roofs of tile, floors of large brick tile.
